assessment.nobel_worthiness: A powerful account of how trade and technological change reshape local labour markets, employment and inequality, with broad influence across economics and public debate.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson provide a coherent, complementary empirical programme linking tasks, trade shocks and distributional consequences.
assessment.maturity: The central findings have been extensively studied over more than a decade and have altered research on structural change.
uncertainties: The relative weight of trade, technology and local adjustment mechanisms remains actively debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Transformative long-run measurement of income and wealth concentration has changed the empirical study of inequality and its historical interpretation.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez built foundational distributional series, while Zucman made distinctive contributions to measuring wealth and offshore holdings.
assessment.maturity: The research programme is mature, globally influential and has generated a durable data infrastructure.
uncertainties: Measurement choices for capital income, wealth and tax avoidance can materially affect levels and trends.
The appropriate laureate allocation within a broad collaborative literature is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection supplied a fundamental explanation for trade patterns, aggregate productivity and unequal effects of globalization.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's framework is central; Helpman and Redding made major complementary theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become a standard building block in international trade and related work on firms and growth.
uncertainties: Credit assignment is difficult because the programme encompasses a large subsequent literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation approach gave a compelling quantitative framework for understanding why similarly endowed economies can have very different productivity levels.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow established the influential empirical-accounting approach, with Restuccia central to its development and extension.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established and has stimulated extensive work on institutions, firms and development.
uncertainties: Inference from revenue productivity to underlying distortions depends on strong modeling and measurement assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data were used to make intergenerational mobility geographically precise and to recast opportunity as a measurable empirical object.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are especially central to the mobility programme; Friedman is a major collaborator in its data and empirical development.
assessment.maturity: The work has already reshaped research and policy discussions, though its full long-run influence is still unfolding.
uncertainties: Causal interpretations of place effects and policy implications remain subject to continuing research.
The leading researchers are comparatively early in their careers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary analysis of routines and organizational capabilities offered a lasting alternative account of innovation, firms and economic dynamism.
assessment.attribution: Winter's intellectual contribution is unusually identifiable within this candidate formulation.
assessment.maturity: The work has had decades to diffuse across organizational economics, innovation studies and management.
uncertainties: Its Nobel attribution is complicated by foundational collaborators not included in this candidate entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their political-economy research clarified how institutions, electoral incentives and state capacity shape fiscal policy and long-run development.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini supplied foundational formal and empirical work, with Besley a major contributor on political incentives and state capacity.
assessment.maturity: This is a mature and influential research tradition with broad application across comparative political economy.
uncertainties: The programme is broad, making a sharply delimited discovery and exhaustive allocation of credit difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods made credible empirical analysis feasible in a wide range of settings with unobserved heterogeneity and endogenous dynamics.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are directly associated with the canonical estimator, while Blundell made a central contribution to the system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding, widely taught and deeply embedded in applied econometric practice.
uncertainties: Widespread use has also exposed finite-sample, instrument-proliferation and specification concerns.
